commit_scope: Keep app.hati.earth honest and usable while its private Sheet balance is loading or recovering from a transient carrier miss.

task_card.goal: Stop a normal or slow Sheet read from being presented as an outage and let the grocery balance recover without a manual reload.
done_when: A fresh load says connecting rather than unavailable before the first Sheet response.
Transient or semantic Sheet misses retry and later recover on online, visible-tab, and quiet interval events.
The production build, full web suite, worktree web/API verifier, CI, deploy, and live browser check pass.

constraints: Do not persist balances or transaction data in browser storage.
Do not log or expose the household token, balance, transaction rows, Sheet secret, or Apps Script URL.
Keep the Sheet Restricted and retain fail-closed semantics after bounded recovery is exhausted.

evidence_refs: A fresh production page load visibly rendered Sheet temporarily unavailable before the initial totals request completed; the same page then rendered the confirmed Sheet balance without configuration or data changes.
The former BalanceCard treated totals=null as an outage, conflating not-yet-read with unavailable.
The former client accepted a 200 totals response with remaining_source=unavailable without a semantic retry or later recovery event.
The client now carries loading, retrying, ready, and unavailable as distinct states and reserves unavailable for exhausted bounded attempts.
A finite balance is accepted only when the API attributes remaining_source to the Sheet.
A last-confirmed balance remains in memory during a transient miss and is explicitly qualified as reconnecting; no financial value is written to localStorage or sessionStorage.
Two token-silent attempts each have a 16-second ceiling, leaving the API's 13-second Sheet/DB boundary room to finish without logging the private query string.

Online, visible-tab, and one-minute visible-page events trigger a fresh Sheet read; ordinary triggers coalesce behind the active read, while a mutation-required fresh read cancels its predecessor before it can consume more Sheet capacity.
The recovery clock detects a Bali calendar-day boundary and refreshes both today's spend rows and the balance, preventing yesterday's rows from remaining beside a new-day total.
A failed new-day spend read leaves that day unconfirmed, so every later online, visible-tab, or interval recovery retries the full board until its entries arrive.
When no totals response arrives, unqualified day/month aggregates clear to an unknown presentation instead of remaining stale; only the explicitly labelled last-confirmed balance is retained.
Transient shop or Sheet-status read failures retain the last good UI state instead of temporarily hiding available controls.
Write-forced and new-day refreshes immediately qualify any retained balance as last-confirmed while the fresh Sheet read is in flight; ordinary background reads retain the no-flicker ready state.
Same-day full-board recovery events coalesce behind one request, while obsolete-day and mutation-superseded board reads are aborted and generation-guarded against late state writes.
New-day and post-mutation entry lists hide stale rows behind explicit bilingual connecting copy until the matching spend read succeeds.
Every coalesced full-board request has a 16-second abort deadline, so a hung spend, Sheet-status, or shops read releases the recovery lane for a later attempt.
A replacement refresh invalidates its same-day confirmation before reading, so failed post-mutation entry reads remain eligible for full-board recovery on every later signal.
The Bali calendar helper adds UTC+8 directly to the instant, independent of browser timezone, and changes day exactly at Bali midnight in direct boundary tests.
A shared board timeout preserves every sibling response that did succeed; only a superseding generation discards all results from an older cycle.

HTTP 401/403 responses are carried separately from Sheet or transport misses: the client aborts private reads, clears stale identity and retained private UI/storage state, and returns to the Hati Suci recovery door.

The Form membership-lookup recipe owns retryable HTTP 503 versus authoritative HTTP 401: its verdict-15 band covers every readable/found combination on Go, Rust, TypeScript, and the production fkwu carrier, preventing graph outages from deleting queued drafts.
A healthy background refresh keeps the ready presentation and changes to retrying only after a real miss, avoiding minute-by-minute status flicker.
No household balance, transaction row, actor token, Sheet secret, or Apps Script URL is recorded in this evidence.

The focused policy proof distinguishes connecting, retrying, last-confirmed, unavailable, and stale-identity outcomes; accepts only finite Sheet-owned balances; proves bounded totals and full-board request intervals; immediately qualifies retained balances during forced reads; coalesces ordinary totals and full-board reads; cancels superseded mutation and obsolete-day refreshes; preserves successful sibling responses when another board request times out; invalidates failed replacement days for later full-board retry; hides stale rows until the matching entry read succeeds; changes day exactly at Bali midnight; clears unqualified stale aggregates after an exhausted read; returns truly unauthorized devices to the identity recovery door; and verifies retained confirmation and stale-generation rejection.
